findings.reason: naming those two owners turns §2g from a new subsystem into an extension of review.py and recovery.py, and removes the risk of a second declaration the existing falsifier does not cover.
findings.text: §2g selects profiles by "a run's changed paths" and declares each profile's required elements "in one place that the prompt and the parser both read", but names neither owner; `reckon/crew/recovery.py:1614` (`_changed_paths_between`) already computes a run's changed paths, and `reckon/crew/review.py:100` (`REVIEW_ITEMS`) with `:82` (`REVIEW_DIMENSIONS`) is already the single declaration that the prompt (`reckon/crew/prompts/review.md`) and the parser both read and that the existing prompt-schema falsifier pins

findings.reason: §11 is a change to the obligation, and without naming obligations.py as the owner it reads as new machinery rather than a modification of the existing duty item.
findings.text: §11 has no write paths and names no owner, while `reckon/crew/obligations.py` already carries the mechanism it describes: `_reflex_review_in_flight` (:106) reads whether the reflex's recorded dispatch still holds a live run, `_queued_review_fields` (:283) composes the queued window, and `_review_duty_item` (:323) decides the review-missing/queued kind — the plan should state whether §11 extends these or adds beside them

findings.reason: a second capability reader beside the owner drifts from it; the image requirement should be a value in capability.py's requirement vocabulary so one refusal mechanism serves both the window-fit and image-fit cases.
findings.text: §6 proposes a dispatch refusal for a lane that cannot read an image, "in the same way a context-fit refusal already rejects a node too large for its window", but places it in a new `reckon/crew/figure_review.py` and prompts a new `figure-review.md` without naming `reckon/capability.py`, which already owns lane/worker capability requirements (`assess_execution_fit` :102, `worker_satisfies` :227, `match_worker` :265, `REQUIREMENT_LEVELS` :23)

findings.reason: the interface_budget rule requires the section to account for the surface it adds; §6 currently presents the added role, prompt and refusal as net-new with no retirement statement.
findings.text: §6 introduces a new reviewer role plus `reckon/crew/prompts/figure-review.md` and a new refusal family (lane lacks image capability) against refusal_families 23, and its text names no existing surface it retires or merges, or why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/crew/review.py` stays the one deep module for the review schema, parser and store, and §4/§2g extend it rather than fanning the behaviour across new wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 adds a capability-based lane refusal without naming what owns capability requirements.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §6 adds a reviewer role, an additional prompt file and a new refusal family for a lane lacking image capability, and names nothing it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2g adds a six-profile subsystem whose two inputs, the run's changed paths and a single prompt/parser element declaration, both already have owners the section does not cite.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — where the plan could have added a parallel path it extends an existing one instead: the review pass joins `resumption.sweep` rather than a new sweep (§3), and §2j reuses the existing `crew check-manifest` verb by adding a prompt instruction rather than a second command.
